fixes.explanation: Counting is the census, and that comes before the hauling. The LORD tells Moses and Aaron to take a census of the Kohathites (Numbers 4:2), so counting is how the men get on the list. The carrying comes later, once Aaron and his sons have covered the holy objects and the camp is ready to move (Numbers 4:15). Getting on the list is one thing, and lifting is another. In my bakery the only thing I lift is a cookie box, and I still wobble.

Shields and spears aren't on the Gershonites' list, friend. They carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting with its covering of fine leather, and the courtyard curtains, plus the ropes and equipment (Numbers 4:25-26). Their load is fabric, and a lot of it. I bet folding that much curtain is a workout all by itself.

False, and verse 49 is why. After the count of 8,580, each man is assigned his work and burden, so it reaches the Gershonites and the Merarites too (Numbers 4:46-49). Three clans, three sets of jobs, and every counted man gets his own assignment. That's a whole lot of names on one list. I'd need a bigger apron just to carry the paperwork.

problems.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
Saying the Kohathites were not doing the counting is too broad. Moses and Aaron, who conducted the census, descended from Kohath (Exodus 6:18–20).
The passage does not say nobody was marching to battle, that there were no battle cries, or that a curtain was swung around.
Papa imagines himself having a task among the counted Levites. He must never place himself in a Bible event.
